newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - July 3.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - July 3.

text.p: News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media & the Internet and Brand-name Products.
PARIS - Publicis SA, the French advertising firm, signs two accords giving the group a 51-percent stake in and control of two Israeli advertising agencies, Ariely and Pelled. (Reuter)

PARIS - French pay television group Canal Plus says it has filed a lawsuit against the French terrestrial television channels and their media-selling units over their refusal to broadcast an advert for Canal Plus last April. (Reuter)

PARIS - A battle has broken out again between France's two rival television groups, private station TF1 and pay TV group Canal Plus. It's the latest of several skirmishes which date from late last year when TPS was launched as TF1's head-on challenge to Canal Plus's virtual monopoly in the French pay television, industry observers say. (Reuter)

PARIS - Gaumont, the French film production and distribution company, said the success of Luc Besson's film, "The Fifth Element", helped push turnover at its film-making division above that of its distribution arm for the first time ever. (Reuter)

DUESSELDORF - The New York headquarters of Euro RSCG, the French-based advertising group, has approved funds for wider investment, paving the way for worldwide expansion, German unit chief executive Gerhard Schoeps says. He also confirmed Euro RSCG won the account for a brand-name campaign for Henniger Braeu, although the brewery's main account will stay with the German Bates unit. (Reuter)

LONDON - Bernard Arnault, the chairman of LVMH, may change tactics in his battle to prevent the planned 24-billion-pound ($39.1-billion) merger between Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc, The Independent newspaper reports. It says Arnault might put forward plans to sell Guinness's brewing arm and GrandMet's Pillsbury and Burger King food businesses to trade buyers rather than spin them off as separate companies. (Reuter)

LONDON - Burger King, the hamburger chain owned by Britain's Grand Metropolitan Plc, says it plans to withdraw from France after a review of its operations in Europe. It has 39 restaurants in France, mainly in and around Paris, of which 23 are owned by franchisees. In Brussels rival fast-food chain Quick, which has a stronger hold in the French market than Burger King, said it was assessing the implications for itself of Burger King's decision to pull out. (Reuter)
PARIS - Sanofi, the pharmaceuticals and beauty products group, says it will unload its 49.9-percent stake in Nina Ricci if the perfume house's founders decide to sell. (Reuter)
